provenance.rationale: **The union of two paths with the same ends, whose interiors are disjoint and anticomplete, is a hole** — the paper's `P₁ ∪ P₂`. The hypotheses `3 ≤ p.length`, `3 ≤ p'.length` say that each path has length `≥ 2`, i.e. has a nonempty interior; without them the "union" is not a cycle at all (two paths of length `1` between the same ends coincide, and a path of length `1` together with a longer one gives a chorded cycle). erratum.title: Theorem 18.3, second conclusion: the parity clause fails for lines of length 1
erratum.problem: The second conclusion of 18.3 (p. 110) says that for every maximal subpath P′ of P with no Y-complete internal vertex, the length of P′ has the same parity as the number of ends of P′ in {p₁, pₙ} that are not Y-complete. A Y-complete edge pᵢpᵢ₊₁ of P is such a maximal subpath: it has no internal vertex, length 1, and no end in {p₁, pₙ} that fails to be Y-complete, so the clause demands 1 ≡ 0. Read literally the sentence therefore forces P to have no Y-complete edge, which contradicts the third conclusion of 18.3 and the paper's own use of it in 18.4 ("P contains an odd number of Y-complete edges"). The paper's proof carries the side condition "let P′ be a line of length ≥ 2", and its recap states the correct trichotomy including "either it has length 1"; the alternative was dropped when the recap became the statement.
erratum.fix: The formalized 18.3 adds the side condition 2 ≤ length of the subpath to the second conclusion, exactly the condition the printed proof uses. The only consumer, 18.5, applies the conclusion with index ≥ 3, so the paper's own uses are unaffected.

erratum.title: Theorem 9.3, outcome 4, is false as printed
erratum.problem: Outcome 4 asks for a vertex f ∈ F with the same neighbours as x₁ in V(P₁) ∪ V(P₂) ∪ V(Q₂) that is not adjacent to y₁. This can fail when Q₁ is long. Let H be the bipartite subdivision of K₄ whose two diagonals become branches of length 4 and 2, let G be the complement of the line graph L(H) on its 10 edges, and add one vertex f with exactly the neighbours of x₁. With the knot P₁ = a₁-b₁, P₂ = a₂-b₂, Q₁ = x₁-z₁-z₂-y₁, Q₂ = x₂-y₂ and F = {f}, every hypothesis of 9.3 holds (G is Berge; G and its complement have no K₄-enlargement appearance and no overshadowed K₄ appearance; the attachments of F are not local), yet all four outcomes fail. Outcome 4 fails because f is adjacent to y₁, exactly as x₁ is.
erratum.fix:
The formalized statement `thm_9_3` weakens the last clause of outcome 4 to "f has a non-neighbour on Q₁ other than x₁" (here z₁). The printed clause implies this one, and the two agree when Q₁ has length 1, so case (1) of the printed proof is untouched; case (2) and everything downstream, up to the main theorem, go through with the weaker outcome.

Lean checks that the four lists form a knot, that f is a twin of x₁, that all four printed outcomes fail, and that neither G nor its complement has a K₄-enlargement appearance, and bundles this as `printed_nine_three_false`.
